summary: Walks a null-terminated char string in place. ASCII digit characters '0'-'9' (48..57) are overwritten with their nibble value (byte minus 48); semicolon characters (59) are removed by left-shifting the remaining characters over them; all other characters pass through unchanged. Used to fold a locale digit-grouping string such as "3;2;1" into a packed nibble array.

operations.description: Initialize the walk pointer v1 to the start of the input string a1.
Seed the loop state with the first character of the string, result = *a1.
Outer loop iterates while the current character *v1 is non-null; each iteration starts from the previously read character in result.
Digit test: when result is in [48, 57] the character is an ASCII digit.
Overwrite the current byte with its nibble value: *v1 = result - 48.
Non-digit branch: when result equals 59 (semicolon), enter the deletion path.
Inner shift loop: starting at the semicolon position, copy each byte from the following position and advance, until a null terminator is copied; this removes the semicolon in place.
Advance the walk pointer by one byte (++v1) after a digit conversion or a passthrough character.
Return the last examined character (the terminating null at normal loop exit).

unresolved: The meaning of the returned character is not consumed by this function; callers decide how it is used.
The exact purpose of the digit-to-nibble conversion depends on the caller-provided grouping string and is not visible here.
